label: Classics — six fields for public-domain and U.S. government works
note: A catalogue extension so the base of public-domain / U.S. government works has fields to be shelved in and bridges to be read across. Only three bridges are declared; metrology stands alone (a one-field compare needs no bridge). Nothing here claims that all fields couple.

fields.label: Natural history (19th-century)
fields.units: descriptive; counts of specimens and varieties
anti_overreach: no claim about any living person
no modern taxonomic claim from a historic text

fields.label: Heredity (19th-century plant hybridisation)
anti_overreach: no clinical or genetic claim from a historic text

fields.label: Optics (17th–19th-century)
anti_overreach: no claim about vision or perception in people

fields.label: Electricity (19th-century experimental)
fields.units: descriptive experimental series; quantities as named by the author
anti_overreach: no claim about any therapeutic use of electricity

fields.label: Electromagnetism (19th-century treatise)
fields.units: field quantities as named by the author
anti_overreach: no claim beyond the text's own definitions

fields.label: Metrology (measurement uncertainty guidance)
anti_overreach: no claim that a guidance document validates any particular measurement

bridges.junction: which counts of varieties in a natural-history text may stand beside which offspring ratios in a hybridisation text, as descriptions of variation only
which experimentally named quantities may stand beside which treatise-defined field quantities, at stated reliability
which optical quantities may stand beside which electromagnetic ones, as the treatise itself relates them

stop.rule: demo stop: abandon at the date whatever the results look like
